name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset of 108,249 real-world images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs to support comprehensive scene understanding.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1, 2016.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The first release uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. For each new image, workers drew bounding boxes and wrote region descriptions iteratively until 50 region descriptions were collected per image, with diversity encouraged by showing similar prior descriptions and enforcing BLEU-based dissimilarity thresholds. After region descriptions were collected, workers extracted objects and grounded them with tight bounding boxes, then added attributes and relationships from the text to form region graphs. Scene graphs were created by combining region graphs and merging co-referenced objects, with worker confirmation for overlapping objects. Workers also wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs. All components then went through verification using majority voting or rapid judgments, and objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were canonicalized to WordNet synsets with worker verification of mappings.
rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator, Web API
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The images are all 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M; these are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users. Raw textual data were freeform worker-generated region descriptions and question-answer pairs collected on Amazon Mechanical Turk.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Region graphs were combined into scene graphs by merging objects from different region graphs that referred to the same object. Objects were considered co-referent when their bounding boxes had high overlap and workers confirmed the match. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools, WordNet lexeme counts, hand-crafted mapping rules, and worker verification.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To collect diverse region descriptions, BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 were enforced against previously written image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions. For object extraction, Stanford's dependency parser was used to automatically extract nouns as suggestions to workers. Bounding boxes were required to satisfy coverage and quality constraints. Descriptions with no objects did not receive region graphs. For canonicalization, noun phrases were extracted with Stanford NLP tools; attributes were normalized by morphology/stemming; relationships were mapped using WordNet sentence frames and root hypernyms, with hand-crafted correction rules and worker verification.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers. For region descriptions, workers drew three bounding boxes and wrote three descriptions per task, iterating across workers until 50 descriptions per image were collected. For objects, one worker extracted all objects from each description and drew a bounding box for each object. For attributes and relationships, workers were shown a region description and its extracted objects and asked to add attributes to objects and connect object pairs with relationships, forming region graphs. Scene graphs were formed by combining region graphs and merging co-referenced objects after worker confirmation. For QA pairs, workers wrote freeform QAs about the whole image and region-based QAs based on selected regions, following rules to start with one of the Ws, avoid ambiguity/speculation, and ensure the question was precisely answerable from the image. Verification used three-worker majority voting for all components except objects, which used rapid judgments.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using majority voting and rapid judgments. All components except objects were verified by three unique workers, and an annotation was added if at least two of three workers judged it factually correct. Objects were verified using a rapid serial visual processing inspired interface for faster judgments. Canonicalization mappings were also sent to Amazon Mechanical Turk with the proposed synset and four alternatives so workers could verify or change the mapping. The paper reports canonicalization precision and recall statistics for objects, attributes, and relationships.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Region descriptions: 50 per image; freeform QA: 8 per image task; region-based QA: around 20 per image; verification: 3 workers per annotation for majority voting.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% were from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries. Ages ranged from 18 to 68, with the majority between 25 and 34 years old. Gender distribution was 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools (CoreNLP); BLEU score computation; WordNet synset mapping heuristics
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the first release of the Visual Genome dataset and notes that the dataset collection effort is ongoing. Further visualizations, API, and additional information are available online. No explicit updating timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator geography (country), age, and gender were collected and reported.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to train and benchmark the next generation of computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, enabling applications such as image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. The paper also notes overrepresentation of certain sports in attributes describing people due to image source bias. Common visual concepts like colors and frequent phrases may dominate descriptions without diversity controls, and the collection process explicitly attempted to reduce such dominance.
rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Some descriptions contain no explicit objects and therefore have no region graphs. Relationship prediction is difficult due to high intra-class variability. Current models evaluated on the dataset still perform poorly on complex image reasoning tasks. The dataset images are somewhat biased toward people and certain sports.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is presented as a general-purpose representation of the visual world for training and benchmarking computer vision models. The paper explicitly discusses use for object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, semantic image retrieval, and cognitive scene understanding and reasoning tasks.
